summary: Close to implementable: the authoring surface, provider and codec are well pinned, but the biggest gap is when JEV_TOKEN is resolved and refused (at flow start or at the first Judge) and where that failure lands.

questions.text: Is JEV_TOKEN resolved and the missing/empty refusal applied eagerly at flow start, or lazily on the first Judge request?
questions.reason: Decides whether non-judging flows need the secret and whether refusal lands before side effects or partway through; the ADR only says keys refuse 'before constructing the provider'.

questions.text: Which side validates that the returned [Answer] matches the JudgeRequest (count, kinds, index and probability ranges), and which failure does a mismatch become?
questions.reason: Ownership of the check and the error type (host ModelFailure vs guest FetchError) are open; the ADR says failure terminates with no partial batch and that the guest retains typed assembly.

questions.text: Are judgement requests and answers recorded anywhere (proposal evidence, run log, replay cache), or are they ephemeral?
questions.reason: Recording would need storage and a persisted format bound to closed-recipe proposals; the ADR only says the codec does not change persisted fact formats.

questions.text: How are non-finite scores (NaN, infinity) handled: rejected as malformed, rejected by the codec, or encoded specially?
questions.reason: Both compilers must agree on the rule and its failure path; the ADR only specifies decimal strings for finite scores.

questions.text: Are existing tools and closed recipes written against the old judgement API migrated in this change, or left to fail root checking?
questions.reason: Determines whether a migration of accepted KB sources or just a compile diagnostic is needed; the ADR rejects a compatibility facade and removes old modules from discovery but says nothing about existing callers.

questions.text: Which existing typed guest request carries Judge: the old judgement request reshaped to upstream types, or a new variant beside the SystemTwo request?
questions.reason: Changes the guest/host frame definitions on both GHC and MicroHs; the ADR says only 'an existing typed guest request' over the existing continuation protocol.

questions.text: Does the host retry or time out failed Jev requests, or does any provider exception end the flow immediately?
questions.reason: Retry or timeout policy adds constants and interacts with cancellation; the ADR says to translate exceptions per the SystemTwo pattern and forbids a configuration registry, but is silent on retries.
